target_customer: Pakistani micro-entrepreneurs selling over WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram, and their end customers
problem: Social media sellers in Pakistan lack wholesale sourcing, delivery, payments and customer service; Markaz provides these so they can resell without upfront investment.
business_model: Reselling marketplace earning margin and fees on wholesale orders, with cash on delivery fulfilment

founders.name: Umair Aslam
founders.background_notes: YC page: 12+ years of product-led growth experience across fintech products in Pakistan and Myanmar.

founders.name: Shoaib Khan
founders.background_notes: Dawn lists the four founders as previously at Telenor, Amazon, Easypaisa and Alipay without assigning employers to each person.

founders.name: Sameel Hayat
founders.background_notes: See the group note on Shoaib Khan.

founders.name: Fawad Hussain
founders.background_notes: YC page: 12+ years of IT solutions experience including telecom operators across South and Southeast Asia.

investors: Angels from Careem, Deloitte, Amazon and Gojek

competitors.name: Zarya
competitors.what: Lahore B2B inventory platform for social sellers, replicating Egypt's Taager model

competitors.name: Bazaar
competitors.what: Pakistani B2B platform for SMEs covering inventory procurement, bookkeeping and financial services
competitors.funding_then: USD 30M Series A, August 2021, total USD 38M

technical_complexity.rationale: Marketplace and app engineering is standard; the hard part is logistics, cash on delivery and returns operations in Pakistan.

defensibility.rationale: Supplier relationships, delivery operations and a reseller base are harder to copy than the app, but similar models like Zarya and Taager were being replicated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copycat takeover found; the company reports operating as Markaz Inc. with Pakistan and US offices.

market_need_then: Pakistan has a young population and heavy WhatsApp and Instagram commerce; investors funded several social commerce startups in late 2021 and 2022, such as Zarya and DealCart.

branding.domain_note: Uses markaz.app; acquisition history not found.

identity.logo: Logo and Urdu tagline Sab kuch, ghar pe (everything at home), per the site

brand_strength.rationale: A local-language word meaning center is relevant, but it is shared with many unrelated Markaz organizations and no brand-specific press or community evidence was found.

pivots.from: Reselling marketplace for social media entrepreneurs
pivots.to: General online shopping marketplace including China factory-direct listings and dropshipping
pivots.why: Not stated; current site describes a broader marketplace

outcome_analysis: Markaz is a four-founder Islamabad team that raised a 2.4M seed led by Indus Valley Capital in May 2022 and grew to about 55 staff. It rides a real shift to social commerce in Pakistan, and its site now describes a broader marketplace. No Series A, layoffs or exit were found; the funding gap since 2022 means the later path is unclear.
notes: Seed confirmed by Dawn and ProPakistani (May 10, 2022); YC page also lists a MAGNiTT November 2022 headline for the same raise. Aggregator totals of 2.0M, 2.5M and 2.9M over 2 rounds conflict and are unverified. Education not found for any founder. Dawn names prior employers for the group only. The pivot entry is inferred from the current site description versus the YC one-liner and is low confidence. The meaning of markaz as center (Urdu, from Arabic) is a dictionary meaning, not a stated company origin. Competition recorded as of the batch (Winter 2022); DealCart and later entrants are excluded.
